SMTC maps to the optical-module signal-integrity node as an underfollowed hypothesis; key survival tests are 800G/1.6T design wins, data-center revenue contribution, inventory normalization, and leverage reduction.

TSEM maps to the specialty silicon-photonics foundry node as an underfollowed hypothesis; the thesis survives only if silicon-photonics customer qualifications and AI datacom foundry demand are material.

VRT and ETN are reference anchors for data-center power, cooling, switchgear, UPS, and critical electrical infrastructure; they should benchmark smaller power/cooling discovery names rather than dominate the underfollowed lane.

PWR maps to grid interconnection, transmission, substation, and utility-infrastructure services as an indirect AI data-center deployment bottleneck candidate; evidence must isolate hyperscaler or data-center pull-through from normal utility capex.

POWL maps to switchgear and power-control systems as an underfollowed data-center electrical-equipment hypothesis; the main evidence gap is the share of backlog and revenue tied to AI data centers versus energy and industrial projects.

MOD maps to precision cooling and thermal-management equipment as an underfollowed AI rack-density hypothesis; evidence needed includes data-center cooling revenue, liquid-cooling product mix, and hyperscaler or colocation customer exposure.

CRWD is a reference benchmark for the AI-security control-plane lane; it should be used to judge smaller security automation candidates but requires verification that AI features drive monetization rather than marketing narrative.

S maps to smaller security automation exposure as an underfollowed software hypothesis; survival tests include AI-assisted workflow usage, ARR contribution, retention, enterprise wins, and path to profitability.

The supplied evidence is strongest for the general AI infrastructure chokepoint framework and weaker for ticker-specific exposure across MTSI, SMTC, TSEM, PWR, POWL, MOD, CRWD, and S. Layer 2C should prioritize primary-source filings, earnings transcripts, customer/design-win disclosures, and market-pricing checks.

summary: Layer 2B maps the candidate chunk into ticker-to-node relationships for AI infrastructure bottlenecks. The chunk splits into four lanes: optical/signal-integrity semiconductors, specialty silicon-photonics foundry, data-center power/cooling/grid infrastructure, and AI-security automation software. Reference leaders such as Vertiv, Eaton, and CrowdStrike are retained as benchmarks, while the underfollowed discovery lane centers on MACOM, Semtech, Tower Semiconductor, Quanta Services, Powell Industries, Modine, and SentinelOne. Evidence quality is strongest for the broad bottleneck logic around optics, power, cooling, and upstream capacity control, but ticker-specific exposure remains uneven and requires primary-source validation before any Layer 3 ranking.
